newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares lower after military warning.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares lower after military warning.

text.p: Turkish shares fell on Monday on concerns about political uncertainty after the country's powerful National Security Council (MGK) issued a strong warning to the ruling Islamists.

The IMKB National-100 ended the morning session down 21 points, or 1.3 percent at 1,591, falling back from a high of 1,621 in early trading. Trade volume stood at 9.54 trillion lira ($77.6 million), compared with 7.21 trillion ($58.6 million) on Friday.
"The decisions of the MGK meeting created uncertainty. These are good opportunities for selling, I expect declines," said Mustafa Karaahmetoglu of Sayilgan Securities.

At Friday's meeting, Turkey's generals warned the Islamist-led government of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan they wanted a government crackdown on what they see as a wave of religious zeal threatening secular democracy.
But dealers said a higher opening at the morning session suggested the security council meeting was not a decisively negative factor.

"There is a feeling of insecurity in the market which can be seen from rising volume in the overnight repo market. MGK results were interpreted in different ways," said Mustafa Yilmaz who owns a brokerage.
"An easing in political tension is needed. Newspapers full of pictures of army generals negatively affect the market," Yilmaz said.
One dealer forecast the main market index could slip back to 1,500 support level during the day.

Bankers said financial markets, less affected by political tension, awaited February inflation data due to be announced on Tuesday. Analysts have forecast a month-on-month rise in consumer prices of 4.5-5.5 percent.
"Financial markets do not seem to have shown much of a reaction to the MGK results, but there is uneasiness," said one banker.
Bond yields were little changed in quiet trade as volume fell ahead of February inflation data. The most heavily traded December 10 paper yielded 96.08 percent, compared to Friday's 96.24 average.

"The probability of yields passing 100 percent depends on escalation in political uncertainty. Yields may near 100 percent if February inflation exceeds 5.5 percent, but may fall towards 90 percent if it comes out less than five percent" said one banker.
"Otherwise, it is unlikely for the yields to reach 97-98 percent because the Treasury's borrowing needs will decline from March onwards," he added.

Overnight money rates remained high at 71.75 percent on continuing cash shortage, versus Friday's 71.88 percent average and the Turkish lira eased against the dollar to 122,900 from Friday's close of 122,410 in line with the dollar/mark parity.
